headline: Connectome-constrained models: wiring claims hinge on controlled physiology and audits
label: Connectome Constrained Model Evaluation
summary: Connectome-derived models are now tested under fault injection, operation audits, and fair physiology tuning to probe structure-function claims.
synthesis: Across these four preprints, the dominant thread is that conclusions about connectome-constrained models depend on how they are evaluated. A closed-loop fault assessment of a fly-connectome spiking controller examines pursuit-escape behaviour under connection deletion. The Functional Preservation Score audits connectome operations (quantisation, alignment, transport, and local plasticity) on C. elegans. A benchmark of a connectome-constrained fly visual model against CNNs, RAFT, and CTRNNs reports efficiency gains alongside adversarial and perceptual-illusion limitations. A test that tunes physiology fairly across wirings finds that some Drosophila structure-function claims hold while others reverse. What is new is explicit attention to unmeasured physiology and to the operations applied to connectomes as sources of inferential error. This framing is dominant rather than universal across the items, since the controller fault study centres on failure modes rather than auditing.
